# Draft:Shay culture

The Shay culture is a medieval archaeological culture of modern day Ethiopia. Approximately dated from the 8th century to the 14th century, Shay culture was primarily centered around the regions of Shewa and South Wollo in the Amhara region at the geographical center of the Ethiopian highlands. Its name derives from the local Shay river of Menz.
Shay culture is characterized by the presence of megalithic burials, including hypogea and tumuli burials, as well as heavily fortifications around significant hilltop settlements. Major sites include Tätär Gur, Meshäle Maryam and Ketetiya.
